title: Minimum Depth of Binary Tree
statement:
You get the `root` of a binary tree. Return the length, counted in nodes, of the shortest downward path that starts at the root and stops at a leaf, a node that has neither a left nor a right child. The root itself counts as 1, and an empty tree has depth `0`.

Note that a node with only one child is not a leaf, so a path may not stop there.
constraints: The tree has between 0 and 10^5 nodes
notes:
## Intuition

The answer is the level of the shallowest leaf. A breadth-first walk visits the tree one level at a time, from the root down, so the first leaf it meets is the one closest to the root and the search can stop right there, without touching the deeper levels. A depth-first recursion also works, but it has to explore every branch before it knows which one is shortest.

## Approach

1. An empty tree has depth `0`.
2. Start with `level = [root]` and `depth = 1`.
3. Walk through the nodes of `level`. The first node with no left and no right child is a leaf on the shallowest level, so return `depth`.
4. Otherwise collect each node's existing children into `next`.
5. When the level is done, make `next` the new `level` and add one to `depth`.

## Example 1, step by step

`root = [3,9,20,null,null,15,7]`. Level 1 is `[3]`; node 3 has two children, so `next = [9, 20]`. Level 2 is `[9, 20]`; node 9 has no children, so it is a leaf and the answer is `2`. Nodes 15 and 7 are never visited.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): every node is visited at most once, and the walk stops at the first leaf.
- Space: O(w), where w is the widest level held in `level` and `next`.

## Pitfalls

- A node with one child is not a leaf. The recursion `1 + min(left, right)` is wrong for `[1,2]`: the missing right child would give depth 1, but the answer is 2.
- Test both children before returning; checking only `node.left === null` stops at half-leaves.
- Return `0` for an empty tree before reading `root.left`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `level` | the nodes at the current depth |
| `next` | their children, the nodes one level deeper |
| `depth` | how many nodes a path from the root to `level` contains |
| `node` | the node being checked |

narration.2: An empty tree has no path at all, so its depth is 0.
narration.3: The first level holds only the root.
narration.4: A path that ends at the root contains one node.
narration.6: Process the tree one level at a time.
narration.7: Collect the nodes of the next level here.
narration.8: Look at every node on the current level, left to right.
narration.9: No children means a leaf; it is on the shallowest level reached so far, so this depth is the answer.
narration.10: Queue the left child for the next level if it exists.
narration.11: Queue the right child for the next level if it exists.
narration.13: Move down to the next level...
narration.16: Not reached for a non-empty tree: the deepest level always contains a leaf.
